header: Head-on with obstacle  ·  take 1 of 1  ·  VLM: Gemini Robotics-ER 2
camera_label: Left: real overhead camera of the simulation (topic /perception/annotated_frame). The red boxes and robot ids were drawn on it by the perception module (M1) during the run.
intro_lines: Two robots meet nose to nose in a narrow aisle between two barriers; there is an obstacle near the west end. When a robot has been stuck for 12 s, the system asks a vision-language model (VLM) what to do, checks the answer, and executes it.
Robots: 2  ·  Model: Gemini Robotics-ER 2 (gemini-robotics-er-2-preview)  ·  Take 1 of 1, recorded 2026-11-15.
Left: real overhead camera of the simulation. Right: the run's own logs, replayed in sync with simulation time.
watch_for: What the model proposes each time it is asked (yellow lines on the right).
What the check does with the model's choice of which robot backs out (orange lines).
Which robot actually backs out on the camera.

captions.text: The two robots drive toward each other under their normal navigation (Nav2).
Trigger: robot_1 has been stuck for 12 s. The system sends the model a text prompt and the current camera image. The wait for the answer plays in real time.
Model's answer (decision 1): both robots reverse (back out). It names no yielder.
Check: no yielder was named, so there is nothing to correct (yield_robot_grounded_from = null).
Both reverses completed. Afterwards the robots drove back toward each other and stopped again.
Trigger again: both robots stuck for 12 s. The model is asked again; this prompt also reports that the reverse completed and the robots stalled again.
Model's answer (decision 2): yield, with robot_1 as the robot that backs out so robot_2 can pass.
Check: robot_1 has only 0.70 m of room to back into (1.08 m needed). The feasibility gate swaps the yielder to robot_2 ('yield re-grounded').
Dispatch: robot_2 is sent 'yield' (back out and pull aside); robot_1 is told to wait.
robot_2 has pulled aside; robot_1 is escorted past it toward its goal.

at.match: robot robot_1 arrived at base goal

captions.text: robot_1 has reached its goal; robot_2 now drives to its own goal.

at.match: robot robot_2 arrived at base goal

outcome.text: Outcome: M3-default resolution (grounder-corrected): the system's check corrected the model's yielder. 2 of 2 robots arrived.

legend: Legend: reverse = back straight out · yield = back out and pull aside so the other robot passes · temporary_wait = hold still · yield_robot_grounded_from = the yielder the model named before a gate swap (null = no swap) · dispatch_order_source=chi = the system's own ordering · 'safety stop … min_distance_violation' (dim) = robots closer than 0.45 m are held still by the safety monitor.
disclosure: Illustrative demo, not controlled experimental evidence. Single take (n = 1).
outro_lines: The model's: decision 1 'reverse' (it ran and did not clear the scene); decision 2 'yield' with robot_1 as the yielder.
The system's: when to ask; the feasibility gate's swap of the yielder to robot_2 (robot_1 had 0.70 m of room to back into, 1.08 m needed); the back-out distances; the escort of robot_1 past robot_2.
So this resolution is grounder-corrected, not VLM-driven. What the uncorrected yield would have done is not shown by this take.
